entity.summary: Register your LLC, corporation or assumed business name with the Idaho Secretary of State; you need a business name, a registered agent in Idaho, and a chosen business structure.
entity.quote: This is where you complete your official business registration with the State of Idaho.

state_tax.summary: Use the Idaho Business Registration (IBR) process for tax permits such as a seller's permit for sales and use tax; with employees you also get a withholding account.
state_tax.quote: Idaho requires businesses to register for certain tax permits using the Idaho Business Registration (IBR) process. These permits include seller’s permits for sales and use taxes

unemployment.summary: When you have employees, the same Idaho Business Registration also sets you up with the Department of Labor (unemployment insurance) and the Industrial Commission.
unemployment.quote: If you have employees, you’ll also get a income tax withholding account and permits from the Idaho Department of Labor and the Industrial Commission.

workers_comp.summary: Every employer must secure workers' comp. Sole proprietors, working partners and LLC members, and some family members are exempt but may elect coverage. Contractor registration also asks for proof of workers' comp or a statement of why it isn't required.
workers_comp.quote: Every employer shall secure the payment of compensation under this law in one (1) of the following ways

residential_building.name: Contractor Registration (Idaho Contractors Board)
residential_building.agency: Idaho Contractors Board (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses)
residential_building.covers: Anyone in the business of contracting in Idaho (residential or commercial), except casual or minor jobs under the dollar limit and trades licensed separately (electrical, plumbing, HVAC).
residential_building.threshold: Single minor projects under $2,000 total are exempt (not if part of a larger project)
prerequisites: Proof of workers' compensation insurance (or a statement why it isn't required)
General liability insurance including products and completed operations of at least $300,000
residential_building.insurance: General liability (including products and completed operations) of at least $300,000 single limit, plus workers' compensation if required
residential_building.summary: Idaho has no contractor exam; instead contractors must register with the Idaho Contractors Board before working. Registration requires proof of general liability insurance and workers' comp (or a reason it isn't required). Small one-off jobs under the dollar limit are exempt.
residential_building.quote: it shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of, or hold himself out as, a contractor within this state without being registered as required in this chapter.

evidence.quote: a general liability policy, including products and completed operations insurance covering the applicant’s construction operations in the sum of not less than three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) single limit.

other satisfactory proof that the applicant has procured and has in effect worker’s compensation insurance or a statement by the contractor as to why such certificate or coverage is not required for the applicant

A person performing work on one (1) undertaking or project considered casual, minor, or inconsequential, whether by one (1) or more contracts, the aggregate contract price of which, for labor and materials and all other items, is less than two thousand dollars ($2,000).

residential_building.note: Public works projects require a separate Idaho public works contractor license (not researched here).

commercial_building.name: Contractor Registration (same as residential)
commercial_building.agency: Idaho Contractors Board (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses)
prerequisites: Proof of workers' compensation insurance (or a statement why it isn't required)
General liability insurance of at least $300,000
commercial_building.insurance: General liability of at least $300,000 plus workers' compensation if required
commercial_building.summary: Commercial contractors register with the Idaho Contractors Board just like residential contractors; there is no separate commercial license for private work.
commercial_building.quote: it shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of, or hold himself out as, a contractor within this state without being registered as required in this chapter.

evidence.quote: a general liability policy, including products and completed operations insurance covering the applicant’s construction operations in the sum of not less than three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) single limit.

electrical.name: Electrical Contractor license; Journeyman, Master and Residential Electrician licenses
electrical.agency: Idaho Electrical Board (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses)
electrical.covers: Electrical contracting businesses and individual electricians.
prerequisites: Contractor: proof of liability insurance of $300,000 and workers' compensation if applicable
Journeyman: registered apprenticeship hours plus approved related instruction, then pass the exam
Master: at least four (4) years as a licensed journeyman
electrical.insurance: Liability insurance of $300,000 and workers' compensation if applicable
electrical.summary: Electrical contractors need a state license and liability insurance. Electricians become journeymen after a registered apprenticeship and exam, and can qualify for master after years as a licensed journeyman.
electrical.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person, partnership, company, firm, association or corporation to act, or attempt to act, as an electrical contractor or limited electrical contractor in this state until such person

evidence.quote: An electrical contractor, prior to being issued a license, shall be required to provide proof of liability insurance in the amount of three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) and proof of worker’s compensation insurance if applicable.
An apprentice electrician, as defined in section 54-1003A , Idaho Code, may take the journeyman’s examination if he has completed the required related instruction for electrical apprentices
Any person who has worked as a licensed journeyman for a period of not less than four (4) years

plumbing.name: Plumbing Contractor / Journeyman Plumber certificate of competency
plumbing.agency: Idaho State Plumbing Board (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses)
plumbing.covers: Anyone engaged in the business or work of plumbing (sewer, excavating and utility contractors excepted).
prerequisites: Pass the state examination for a certificate of competency
Apprentice registration and hours for journeyman
plumbing.summary: Plumbing work in Idaho requires a state certificate of competency, earned by passing the Plumbing Board's exam; plumbing businesses need a responsible person who holds one.
plumbing.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person or firm, copartnership, association or corporation, to engage in the business, trade, practice or work of plumbing in this state after the adoption of this chapter, unless such person, or responsible person representing such firm, copartnership, association or corporation, has successfully passed an examination
plumbing.note: Experience hours are set by Board rule (not confirmed here).

mechanical.name: HVAC Contractor / Journeyman / Specialty certificate of competency
mechanical.agency: Idaho HVAC Board (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses)
mechanical.covers: Anyone engaged in the business or work of heating, ventilation and air conditioning.
prerequisites: Pass the HVAC Board exam for a certificate of competency
Journeyman: approved related instruction and required apprentice hours
mechanical.summary: HVAC work requires a state certificate of competency from the HVAC Board; journeymen qualify through apprenticeship hours and instruction before taking the exam.
mechanical.quote: it shall be unlawful for any person or firm, copartnership, association or corporation to engage in the business, trade, practice or work of heating, ventilation and air conditioning in this state unless such person or responsible person representing such firm, copartnership, association or corporation, has successfully passed an examination

evidence.quote: may take the journeyman’s examination if the apprentice has completed the required related instruction for a heating, ventilation and air conditioning apprentice

roofing.covers: Roofers register as contractors like any other construction business.
roofing.summary: Idaho has no separate roofing license; roofing businesses need the general Idaho contractor registration.
roofing.quote: it shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of, or hold himself out as, a contractor within this state without being registered as required in this chapter.

pesticide.name: Professional Pesticide Applicator license
pesticide.covers: Anyone applying pesticides as a professional applicator (for hire), including lawn, tree and structural pest control.
prerequisites: At least eighteen years of age
pesticide.insurance: Proof of financial responsibility as set by rule
pesticide.summary: Professional pesticide applicators need a license from the Idaho State Department of Agriculture, which requires passing the department's exam and showing financial responsibility.
pesticide.quote: No person shall act as a professional applicator without first obtaining a professional applicator’s license issued by the department.

evidence.quote: An applicant must be at least eighteen (18) years of age and must pass the department’s examination
Show proof of financial responsibility as prescribed by rule

asbestos.name: Federal asbestos NESHAP notification (no state contractor license found)
asbestos.agency: U.S. EPA Region 10 (most buildings); Idaho DEQ (Tier 1 major facilities)
asbestos.covers: Demolitions and renovations disturbing regulated asbestos-containing material.
prerequisites: 10-working-day Asbestos NESHAP notification before demolition or qualifying renovation
asbestos.summary: No Idaho asbestos contractor license was found. All demolitions and qualifying renovations need the federal Asbestos NESHAP notification, sent to EPA Region 10 for most buildings.
asbestos.quote: All demolition projects require submittal of the Asbestos NESHAP 10-Day Renovation and Demolition Notification Form .

evidence.quote: EPA Region 10 has jurisdiction over all nonmajor facilities (e.g., public, commercial, and institutional structures)

asbestos.note: Federal EPA/OSHA asbestos training rules still apply.

lead_rrp.name: EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm and Certified Renovator
lead_rrp.covers: Anyone paid to disturb paint in homes, child care facilities and preschools built before 1978.
lead_rrp.summary: Idaho does not run its own RRP program, so renovation firms get lead-safe certification directly from EPA.
lead_rrp.quote: EPA administers the RRP Program in most Tribes, states and territories, but has authorized the following to operate their own programs: Alabama, Delaware, Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Massachusetts, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin

evidence.quote: EPA's RRP Rule requires that anyone paid to perform work that disturbs painted surfaces in homes, childcare facilities and preschools built before 1978 be certified and their employees be trained
